gold.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email with a case-sensitive exact match and no normalisation, so changing the letter case of a blocked address bypasses the block list.

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: should_block? looks up `where(email: email)` with an exact, case-sensitive match, and User.new_from_params passes the submitted email through without downcasing it. A blocked address like `bad@spammers.org` can sign up as `Bad@Spammers.org`. Fix: normalize case before comparing, e.g. `where('lower(email) = ?', email.to_s.downcase)`, and store blocked emails in lowercase.

gold.comment: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example, 50 members gives 2 pages). The `next` action can then set offset to user_count, which shows an empty last page, and `showingLast` is false on the real last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` for totalPages. Also make `next` stop when `offset + limit >= user_count`.

gold.comment: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

finding.suggestionContent: `record_for_host` queries on `uri.host`, which excludes the port. The validation regex allows an optional `:port`, so a host saved as `example.com:8080` never matches any referer or embed URL. Embedding is silently denied for those entries. Either reject ports in the validation, or match on `host:port` when the URI has a non-default port.

finding.label: performance
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, whose `poll_feed` loops over every `rss.items` entry with no early exit after the requested `embed_url` is imported. WHY: A single embed request for an unknown URL synchronously re-imports the whole feed (each item runs `TopicEmbed.import` → DB lookups / topic+post creation), so a feed with N items produces O(N) heavy writes per embed view, even when the desired item is the first one. HOW: Let `poll_feed` break out of the loop once `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, or pass the target embed_url into the job so it only processes matching items.

+class TopicRetriever
+
+  def initialize(embed_url, opts=nil)
+    @embed_url = embed_url
+    @opts = opts || {}
+  end
+
+  def retrieve
+    perform_retrieve unless (invalid_host? || retrieved_recently?)
+  end
+
+  private
+
+    def invalid_host?
+      SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host
+    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
+      # An invalid URI is an invalid host
+      true
+    end
+
+    def retrieved_recently?
+      # We can disable the throttle for some users, such as staff
+      return false if @opts[:no_throttle]
+
+      # Throttle other users to once every 60 seconds
+      retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}"
+      if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
+        $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
+        return false
+      end
+
+      true
+    end
+
+    def perform_retrieve
+      # It's possible another process or job found the embed already. So if that happened bail out.
+      return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
+
+      # First check RSS if that is enabled
+      if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
+        Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
+        return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
+      end
+
+      fetch_http
+    end
+
+    def fetch_http
+      user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first
+      return if user.blank?
+
+      TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)
+    end
+
+end

gold.comment: The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

finding.label: performance
finding.suggestionContent: Any anonymous request with an unseen embed_url enqueues RetrieveTopic, and the throttle is keyed only on the exact URL. Each distinct path on the embeddable host therefore triggers a full RSS download and import (TopicRetriever calls PollFeed synchronously) plus a remote HTTP fetch. That is unbounded job and network fanout from unauthenticated traffic. Rate-limit enqueueing per IP or globally, and run the feed poll at most once per interval instead of once per retrieval.

gold.comment: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as well as MANAGE, so an admin with only view permission on all groups passes manage checks such as group creation.

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: canManage() (no-arg) authorizes on AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW as well as MANAGE — `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` — making it identical to canView(). WHY: hasPermission accepts any of the given scopes, so a subject granted only the all-groups VIEW permission is considered able to MANAGE all groups; GroupsResource.createGroup and other manage endpoints call groups().requireManage()/canManage(), so a read-only group viewer can create/update/delete groups (privilege escalation). The sibling canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) correctly uses MANAGE only, and UserPermissionsV2.canManage uses MANAGE only, confirming this is an unintended copy of canView. HOW: return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);

gold.comment: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: getClientsWithPermission looks up resources by type AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients") and adds resource.getName(), but V2 per-client resources are created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource without any setType, so findByType("Clients") never matches them. WHY: the only resource that can match is the 'all-clients' type resource whose name is the literal "Clients", so the method never returns actual client IDs and instead pollutes the result with "Clients" (or an empty set), breaking its caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229 which uses the returned values as client IDs. HOW: either set the CLIENTS resource type on per-client resources when they are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, or resolve the client resources as V1 does (find the per-client resources and map to client.getClientId()).

Evaluate the concrete client resource before falling back to the all-clients resource, and do not expose a global listing shortcut when individual denials must be honored.

gold.comment: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authorization resource id instead of the resource name (the group id) for both the permission check and the returned set, so per-group view-members grants are not resolved and user filtering gets wrong ids.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses groupResource.getId() as the group identifier. Group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() are named with the group id, while Resource.getId() is the internal resource UUID. The returned set therefore contains resource UUIDs instead of group ids, causing UserModel.GROUPS filtering to match no users and causing the per-resource permission check in hasPermission to fall back to the all-groups resource. Use groupResource.getName() to obtain the group id.

gold.comment: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

gold.comment: SMS-sending locks are counted as failed scheduling attempts: scheduleSMS returns undefined for locked users/teams, retryCount is incremented, and after two cron runs the retryCount > 1 cleanup deletes future reminders even if sending is later unlocked.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `else` branch increments retryCount whenever `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value, but `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` (not an error) whenever SMS sending is locked for the user/team (`isLockedForSMSSending`, twilioProvider.ts:79-95). WHY: A temporary lock (user or any team membership with smsLockState LOCKED) is misclassified as a send failure; combined with the top `deleteMany({ OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] })`, the reminder is permanently deleted after two cron runs instead of being retried once the lock is lifted, silently dropping a valid reminder. HOW: only increment retryCount on a genuine send error (keep the increment in the catch block) and handle the locked/skipped return without counting it as a failure.

gold.comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` unconditionally sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the parsed response has no `refresh_token`.
WHY: `office365calendar` uses `refreshTokenResponseSchema` in which `refresh_token` is optional (CalendarService.ts:56) and then does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` (CalendarService.ts:264) before persisting. When the provider's refresh response omits `refresh_token`, this literal now overwrites the still-valid stored refresh token, so the next refresh attempt sends `refresh_token="refresh_token"` and permanently fails — the previous raw `safeParse` path preserved the old refresh token. HOW: only inject the placeholder when the caller's flow actually needs it (sharing/sync path), e.g. pass a flag or restrict the injection to the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` branch, and never overwrite an existing `refresh_token` in the non-sharing branch.

WHY: Splits/merges multiple same-day overrides into wrong unavailable verdict. HOW: First find matching-day override(s), then test containment without mixing overrides.

gold.comment: The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that start within working hours but end after them are accepted.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable has two defects. `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so the end bound is never checked and a slot that overruns the working hours is accepted. The `find` also returns true for any single working-hour entry that does not contain the slot, so a host with several entries on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) has every slot rejected. Fix: compute `end` from `slotEndTime`, and reject only if no entry on that day contains the whole slot (use `some` containment, not `find` on non-containment).

gold.comment: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with `&&`, so a team admin who is not an owner is denied. Use `||` so either role is authorized.

gold.comment: Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Office365 createEvent always selects the first host's destination even when EventManager invokes it with another host's credential. Collective bookings therefore POST to the organizer's calendar ID using the co-host's token instead of creating the co-host's event, causing calendar creation to fail. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and select the destination matching that credential.

gold.comment: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for the weekday excludes it, so split schedules (e.g. morning and afternoon) reject all slots.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The slot is rejected if any working-hours entry for that weekday fails to contain it, so a schedule with several ranges on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) rejects every slot, because each slot is outside at least one range. Fixed hosts with split working days lose all availability. Reject only when no applicable range contains the slot, e.g. `!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`.

gold.comment: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The catch-block increment also uses stale reminder.retryCount + 1. WHY: Same lost-update race as the else branch — concurrent failures undercount retries. HOW: Use atomic increment.

gold.comment: When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The recurring-cancel block now sits inside the loop over every calendar reference. It deletes all updated bookings' events through all of the organizer's credentials once per reference, so the same events are deleted N times (the duplicates fail or produce errors). Other hosts' events are still not deleted through their own credentials. Run the recurring bulk delete once, outside the per-reference loop, or scope it to the current reference's credential.

gold.comment: The override timezone conversion keeps only hour and minute, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone become inverted ranges or are applied to the wrong day.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: startTime/endTime are taken as `hour()*60+minute()` after shifting by the timezone offset, so a converted override that crosses midnight wraps around (e.g. 20:00-23:00 shifted by +6h becomes 02:00-05:00 while still attached to the original day, or a range where endTime < startTime). This produces slots on the wrong day or no slots at all. Compute minutes relative to `startOfInviteeDay` (e.g. `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).diff(startOfInviteeDay, 'minute')`) instead of taking time-of-day modulo 24h.

gold.comment: Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The Salesforce service now calls login.salesforce.com to refresh the token on every client creation. It does this directly instead of through `refreshOAuthTokens`, and it keys the failure check on `response.statusText !== 'OK'`. With credential sync enabled, it ignores the external sync endpoint and uses Cal.com's own client credentials. It also adds a network round trip and a DB write to every use of the service, and an empty statusText (for example over HTTP/2) is treated as an error. Wrap the fetch in `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, check `response.ok`, and refresh only when the access token is missing or expired.

gold.comment: The retry-count update inside the catch block is not guarded, so if it throws (for example the reminder was deleted concurrently) the error escapes the loop and the cron run fails, skipping the remaining reminders.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The catch block now performs an unprotected `prisma.workflowReminder.update`. If this update throws (e.g., record already deleted by a concurrent cron run or a transient DB error), the error propagates out of the catch block, aborts the for loop, and fails the entire cron handler. Wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch or move the log before the update so a persistence failure does not crash the batch.

gold.comment: In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The changed line now allows `selectedCalendar` to be undefined (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but the later conference-data `calendar.events.patch` call still passes the raw `selectedCalendar` as `calendarId`. WHY: When `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` is empty (common), the insert succeeds on "primary" but the follow-up patch is sent with an undefined calendarId, so the Google Meet hangout link patch fails/targets the wrong calendar. HOW: pass `selectedCalendar || "primary"` (or a resolved variable) to the patch call as well.

gold.comment: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now awaits twilio.cancelSMS before the prisma delete in the same try block, so a Twilio failure skips the DB delete. WHY: Previously the caller deleted the reminder row independently even when the Twilio cancel threw (manager swallowed), but now a transient Twilio error leaves a scheduled SMS row with no cancelled flag and no retry, so the SMS is still sent for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. HOW: Delete the row independently of Twilio result (or mark cancelled and retry), e.g. move the prisma delete outside the Twilio try or into a finally.

gold.comment: After deleting the calendar cache, CredentialActionsDropdown does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so where no parent refetch callback is passed the stale cache status and delete action remain visible.

If the parent `onChanged` does not refetch, the dropdown continues to display the old `cacheUpdatedAt` after a successful deletion. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess`, matching the behavior of `disconnectMutation`.

gold.comment: Each import(...) in the appStore object literal runs when app-store/index.ts is imported, so all integrations still load at startup instead of lazily, while every entry becomes a promise.

finding.label: performance

Any caller of getCalendar, getVideoAdapters or the payment lookups still pulls in every app's dependencies (Google, Office365, Stripe, etc.) at module load. To make the loading lazy, wrap each entry in a thunk, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call it at the use sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

gold.comment: When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: When useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gets skipToken (rule undefined), loading is false, so MaybeSupported is AlwaysSupported and Duplicate becomes `toAbility(AlwaysSupported, grafana create permission)`. AlertRuleMenu ORs this into canDuplicate for every non-Grafana (data-source) rule, so Duplicate is enabled whenever the user can create Grafana rules, even if the ruler ability says no. Fix: when `rule` is undefined, return NotSupported for every ability (for example `const MaybeSupported = !rule || loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`).

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import queue
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import defaultdict
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar
+
+import sentry_sdk
+from arroyo.backends.kafka.consumer import KafkaPayload
+from arroyo.processing.strategies import ProcessingStrategy
+from arroyo.types import BrokerValue, FilteredPayload, Message, Partition
+
+from sentry.utils import metrics
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):
+    """Work item that includes the original message for offset tracking."""
+
+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T
+    message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]
+
+
+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:
+                        break
+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable
+
+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}
+
+
+class OrderedQueueWorker(threading.Thread, Generic[T]):
+    """Worker thread that processes items from a queue in order."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        worker_id: int,
+        work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]],
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        offset_tracker: OffsetTracker,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(daemon=True)
+        self.worker_id = worker_id
+        self.work_queue = work_queue
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.offset_tracker = offset_tracker
+        self.shutdown = False
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        """Process items from the queue in order."""
+        while not self.shutdown:
+            try:
+                work_item = self.work_queue.get()
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+
+            try:
+                with sentry_sdk.start_transaction(
+                    op="queue_worker.process",
+                    name=f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}",
+                ):
+                    self.result_processor(self.identifier, work_item.result)
+
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception(
+                    "Unexpected error in queue worker", extra={"worker_id": self.worker_id}
+                )
+            finally:
+                self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+                metrics.gauge(
+                    "remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth",
+                    self.work_queue.qsize(),
+                    tags={
+                        "identifier": self.identifier,
+                    },
+                )
+
+
+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Fixed pool of queues that guarantees order within groups.
+
+    Key properties:
+    - Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue
+    - Each queue has exactly one worker thread
+    - Items within a queue are processed in FIFO order
+    - No dynamic reassignment that could break ordering
+    - Tracks offset completion for safe commits
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        num_queues: int = 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.num_queues = num_queues
+        self.offset_tracker = OffsetTracker()
+        self.queues: list[queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]]] = []
+        self.workers: list[OrderedQueueWorker[T]] = []
+
+        for i in range(num_queues):
+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,
+                identifier=identifier,
+                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
+            )
+            worker.start()
+            self.workers.append(worker)
+
+    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
+        """
+        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
+        """
+        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues
+
+    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
+        """
+        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
+        """
+        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
+        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]
+
+        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+        work_queue.put(work_item)
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Get statistics about queue depths."""
+        queue_depths = [q.qsize() for q in self.queues]
+        return {
+            "queue_depths": queue_depths,
+            "total_items": sum(queue_depths),
+        }
+
+    def wait_until_empty(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bool:
+        """Wait until all queues are empty. Returns True if successful, False if timeout."""
+        start_time = time.time()
+        while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
+            if self.get_stats()["total_items"] == 0:
+                return True
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        return False
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        """Gracefully shutdown all workers."""
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.shutdown = True
+
+        for q in self.queues:
+            try:
+                q.shutdown(immediate=False)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error shutting down queue")
+
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.join(timeout=5.0)
+
+
+class SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy(ProcessingStrategy[KafkaPayload], Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Processing strategy that uses a fixed pool of queues.
+
+    Guarantees:
+    - Items for the same group are processed in order
+    - No item is lost or processed out of order
+    - Natural backpressure when queues fill up
+    - Only commits offsets after successful processing
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        queue_pool: FixedQueuePool[T],
+        decoder: Callable[[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], T | None],
+        grouping_fn: Callable[[T], str],
+        commit_function: Callable[[dict[Partition, int]], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self.queue_pool = queue_pool
+        self.decoder = decoder
+        self.grouping_fn = grouping_fn
+        self.commit_function = commit_function
+        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
+
+        self.commit_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._commit_loop, daemon=True)
+        self.commit_thread.start()
+
+    def _commit_loop(self) -> None:
+        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
+            try:
+                self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)
+
+                committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()
+
+                if committable:
+                    metrics.incr(
+                        "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed",
+                        len(committable),
+                        tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+                    )
+
+                    self.commit_function(committable)
+                    for partition, offset in committable.items():
+                        self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.mark_committed(partition, offset)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error in commit loop")
+
+    def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
+        try:
+            result = self.decoder(message.payload)
+
+            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
+            partition = message.value.partition
+            offset = message.value.offset
+
+            if result is None:
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)

+
+            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)
+
+            work_item = WorkItem(
+                partition=partition,
+                offset=offset,
+                result=result,
+                message=message,
+            )

+            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)
+
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")

+                )

+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+
+    def poll(self) -> None:
+        stats = self.queue_pool.get_stats()
+        metrics.gauge(
+            "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued",
+            stats["total_items"],
+            tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def terminate(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()

finding.suggestionContent: In join(), when a timeout is supplied and the deadline elapses on an early process, the loop `break`s, so every remaining process is neither waited on nor `terminate()`d. The previous implementation always ran `self.process.terminate()` after the wait. A hung process past the deadline is now leaked (only reaped at interpreter exit) instead of being killed. Continue iterating to terminate the remaining processes (or terminate all after the wait loop) rather than breaking out.

+
+import logging
+import queue
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import defaultdict
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar

+from arroyo.processing.strategies import ProcessingStrategy
+from arroyo.types import BrokerValue, FilteredPayload, Message, Partition
+
+from sentry.utils import metrics
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):
+    """Work item that includes the original message for offset tracking."""
+
+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T
+    message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]
+
+
+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:

+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable
+
+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}

+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        num_queues: int = 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.num_queues = num_queues
+        self.offset_tracker = OffsetTracker()
+        self.queues: list[queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]]] = []
+        self.workers: list[OrderedQueueWorker[T]] = []
+
+        for i in range(num_queues):
+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,
+                identifier=identifier,
+                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
+            )
+            worker.start()
+            self.workers.append(worker)
+
+    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
+        """
+        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
+        """
+        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues
+
+    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
+        """
+        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
+        """
+        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
+        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]
+
+        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+        work_queue.put(work_item)
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Get statistics about queue depths."""
+        queue_depths = [q.qsize() for q in self.queues]
+        return {
+            "queue_depths": queue_depths,
+            "total_items": sum(queue_depths),
+        }
+
+    def wait_until_empty(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bool:
+        """Wait until all queues are empty. Returns True if successful, False if timeout."""
+        start_time = time.time()
+        while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
+            if self.get_stats()["total_items"] == 0:
+                return True
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        return False
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        """Gracefully shutdown all workers."""
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.shutdown = True
+
+        for q in self.queues:
+            try:
+                q.shutdown(immediate=False)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error shutting down queue")
+
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.join(timeout=5.0)

+class SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy(ProcessingStrategy[KafkaPayload], Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Processing strategy that uses a fixed pool of queues.
+
+    Guarantees:
+    - Items for the same group are processed in order
+    - No item is lost or processed out of order
+    - Natural backpressure when queues fill up
+    - Only commits offsets after successful processing
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        queue_pool: FixedQueuePool[T],
+        decoder: Callable[[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], T | None],
+        grouping_fn: Callable[[T], str],
+        commit_function: Callable[[dict[Partition, int]], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self.queue_pool = queue_pool
+        self.decoder = decoder
+        self.grouping_fn = grouping_fn
+        self.commit_function = commit_function
+        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
+
+        self.commit_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._commit_loop, daemon=True)
+        self.commit_thread.start()
+
+    def _commit_loop(self) -> None:
+        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
+            try:
+                self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)
+
+                committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()
+
+                if committable:
+                    metrics.incr(
+                        "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed",
+                        len(committable),
+                        tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+                    )
+
+                    self.commit_function(committable)
+                    for partition, offset in committable.items():
+                        self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.mark_committed(partition, offset)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error in commit loop")
+
+    def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
+        try:
+            result = self.decoder(message.payload)
+
+            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
+            partition = message.value.partition
+            offset = message.value.offset
+
+            if result is None:
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
+                return
+
+            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)
+
+            work_item = WorkItem(
+                partition=partition,
+                offset=offset,
+                result=result,
+                message=message,
+            )
+
+            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)
+
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")
+            if isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue):
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+
+    def poll(self) -> None:
+        stats = self.queue_pool.get_stats()
+        metrics.gauge(
+            "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued",
+            stats["total_items"],
+            tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def terminate(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def join(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
+        self.close()

gold.comment: The strategy invokes Arroyo's commit callback from a background thread rather than from submit/poll on the consumer thread, so commits can race with polling and partition revocation on a non-thread-safe consumer.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: `commit_function` (Arroyo's commit callback) is called from a background thread. That callback mutates StreamProcessor and Kafka consumer state, and it is meant to be called from the processor's main thread. Running it concurrently with `poll`/`_run_once` can race, and it can also commit for partitions that have just been revoked. Fix: have the commit thread only compute committable offsets and hand them to the main thread, so `commit` is called from `poll()`/`submit()`. Alternatively, guard commits with a lock shared with the main thread and drop them once the strategy is closed.

+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int

+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:
+                        break
+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable
+
+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}

+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):

+    Fixed pool of queues that guarantees order within groups.

+    Key properties:
+    - Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue

+        for i in range(num_queues):

+            self.queues.append(work_queue)

+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import queue
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import defaultdict
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar
+
+import sentry_sdk
+from arroyo.backends.kafka.consumer import KafkaPayload
+from arroyo.processing.strategies import ProcessingStrategy
+from arroyo.types import BrokerValue, FilteredPayload, Message, Partition
+
+from sentry.utils import metrics
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):
+    """Work item that includes the original message for offset tracking."""
+
+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T
+    message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]
+
+
+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:
+                        break
+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable
+
+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}
+
+
+class OrderedQueueWorker(threading.Thread, Generic[T]):
+    """Worker thread that processes items from a queue in order."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        worker_id: int,
+        work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]],
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        offset_tracker: OffsetTracker,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(daemon=True)
+        self.worker_id = worker_id
+        self.work_queue = work_queue
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.offset_tracker = offset_tracker
+        self.shutdown = False
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        """Process items from the queue in order."""
+        while not self.shutdown:
+            try:
+                work_item = self.work_queue.get()
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+
+            try:
+                with sentry_sdk.start_transaction(
+                    op="queue_worker.process",
+                    name=f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}",
+                ):
+                    self.result_processor(self.identifier, work_item.result)
+
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception(
+                    "Unexpected error in queue worker", extra={"worker_id": self.worker_id}
+                )
+            finally:
+                self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+                metrics.gauge(
+                    "remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth",
+                    self.work_queue.qsize(),
+                    tags={
+                        "identifier": self.identifier,
+                    },
+                )
+
+
+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Fixed pool of queues that guarantees order within groups.
+
+    Key properties:
+    - Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue
+    - Each queue has exactly one worker thread
+    - Items within a queue are processed in FIFO order
+    - No dynamic reassignment that could break ordering
+    - Tracks offset completion for safe commits
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        num_queues: int = 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.num_queues = num_queues
+        self.offset_tracker = OffsetTracker()
+        self.queues: list[queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]]] = []
+        self.workers: list[OrderedQueueWorker[T]] = []
+
+        for i in range(num_queues):
+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,
+                identifier=identifier,
+                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
+            )
+            worker.start()
+            self.workers.append(worker)
+
+    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
+        """
+        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
+        """
+        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues
+
+    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
+        """
+        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
+        """
+        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
+        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]
+
+        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+        work_queue.put(work_item)
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Get statistics about queue depths."""
+        queue_depths = [q.qsize() for q in self.queues]
+        return {
+            "queue_depths": queue_depths,
+            "total_items": sum(queue_depths),
+        }
+
+    def wait_until_empty(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bool:
+        """Wait until all queues are empty. Returns True if successful, False if timeout."""
+        start_time = time.time()
+        while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
+            if self.get_stats()["total_items"] == 0:
+                return True
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        return False
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        """Gracefully shutdown all workers."""
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.shutdown = True
+
+        for q in self.queues:
+            try:
+                q.shutdown(immediate=False)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error shutting down queue")
+
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.join(timeout=5.0)
+
+
+class SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy(ProcessingStrategy[KafkaPayload], Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Processing strategy that uses a fixed pool of queues.
+
+    Guarantees:
+    - Items for the same group are processed in order
+    - No item is lost or processed out of order
+    - Natural backpressure when queues fill up
+    - Only commits offsets after successful processing
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        queue_pool: FixedQueuePool[T],
+        decoder: Callable[[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], T | None],
+        grouping_fn: Callable[[T], str],
+        commit_function: Callable[[dict[Partition, int]], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self.queue_pool = queue_pool
+        self.decoder = decoder
+        self.grouping_fn = grouping_fn
+        self.commit_function = commit_function
+        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
+
+        self.commit_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._commit_loop, daemon=True)
+        self.commit_thread.start()
+
+    def _commit_loop(self) -> None:
+        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
+            try:
+                self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)
+
+                committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()
+
+                if committable:
+                    metrics.incr(
+                        "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed",
+                        len(committable),
+                        tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+                    )
+
+                    self.commit_function(committable)
+                    for partition, offset in committable.items():
+                        self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.mark_committed(partition, offset)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error in commit loop")
+
+    def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
+        try:
+            result = self.decoder(message.payload)
+
+            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
+            partition = message.value.partition
+            offset = message.value.offset
+
+            if result is None:
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
+                return
+
+            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)
+
+            work_item = WorkItem(
+                partition=partition,
+                offset=offset,
+                result=result,
+                message=message,
+            )
+
+            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)
+
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")
+            if isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue):
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+
+    def poll(self) -> None:
+        stats = self.queue_pool.get_stats()
+        metrics.gauge(
+            "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued",
+            stats["total_items"],
+            tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def terminate(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def join(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
+        self.close()

gold.comment: Claims zpopmin eviction can drop the root span while the has-root flag stays set, flushing a segment without its root.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The eviction `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` drops spans purely by lowest end_timestamp_precise and never exempts the segment/root span. WHY: When a segment accumulates more than 1000 spans, a root span (notably an is_remote segment span, or any span whose end_timestamp_precise is earlier than its children due to clock skew) is evicted from the sorted set, so done_flush_segments ships a segment with no root/segment span, breaking downstream segment reconstruction. HOW: Before calling zpopmin, compute the segment span member (the payload whose span_id == set_span_id) and re-insert/exclude it (e.g. ZRANGEBYSCORE for `span_count - 1000` victims, remove all but the segment span, and ZADD the retained segment span back) so the root is always preserved.

gold.comment: ZUNIONSTORE merges sorted sets with the default SUM aggregate, so a span payload present in both keys gets a doubled end-timestamp score and is wrongly kept by the oldest-first eviction.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: ZUNIONSTORE is called without AGGREGATE, so it uses the default SUM. A payload present in both the target set and the merged set gets its scores added together, for example a redelivered or duplicated span. Its score is then no longer its end timestamp, so it roughly doubles and is effectively never evicted, which breaks the oldest-first eviction order. Add `"AGGREGATE", "MAX"` (or MIN) to both zunionstore calls.

gold.comment: `import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: import_remote performs a server-side fetch with `open(url)` on the attacker-controllable embed_url that reaches it from the public /embed/best endpoint (EmbedController#best → Jobs::RetrieveTopic → TopicRetriever#fetch_http). The only validation, TopicRetriever#invalid_host? (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15), compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to embeddable_host and ignores port, path, scheme and redirects, and `open` (open-uri) follows HTTP redirects. This allows SSRF: a crafted embed_url such as http://eviltrout.com:6379/... or a redirect from the embeddable host to an internal address makes the server fetch arbitrary internal resources. Validate scheme/port, reject private IPs, and disable redirects (or use a hardened HTTP client with a timeout).

+#
+# Creates and Updates Topics based on an RSS or ATOM feed.
+#
+require 'digest/sha1'
+require_dependency 'post_creator'
+require_dependency 'post_revisor'
+require 'open-uri'
+
+module Jobs
+  class PollFeed < Jobs::Scheduled
+    recurrence { hourly }
+    sidekiq_options retry: false
+
+    def execute(args)
+      poll_feed if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? &&
+                   SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? &&
+                   SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?
+    end
+
+    def feed_key
+      @feed_key ||= "feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"
+    end
+
+    def poll_feed
+      user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first
+      return if user.blank?
+
+      require 'simple-rss'
+      rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)
+
+      rss.items.each do |i|
+        url = i.link
+        url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//
+
+        content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)

+      end

gold.comment: Claims OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets requires every integer offset to exist, so Kafka offset gaps permanently block commits for the partition and per-partition state is never cleared on rebalance.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: get_committable_offsets only moves forward while every offset in the range is present in all_offsets, so it stops at any offset that was never delivered. Kafka partitions can have legitimate offset gaps (transaction control markers, log compaction), so after one gap the partition never commits again and the consumer lag grows forever. Fix: track offsets in submission order (for example, an ordered deque per partition) and commit up to the last completed offset that has no earlier outstanding entry, rather than requiring numerically contiguous offsets.

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import queue
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import defaultdict
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar
+
+import sentry_sdk
+from arroyo.backends.kafka.consumer import KafkaPayload
+from arroyo.processing.strategies import ProcessingStrategy
+from arroyo.types import BrokerValue, FilteredPayload, Message, Partition
+
+from sentry.utils import metrics
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):
+    """Work item that includes the original message for offset tracking."""
+
+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T
+    message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]
+
+
+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:
+                        break
+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable
+
+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}
+
+
+class OrderedQueueWorker(threading.Thread, Generic[T]):
+    """Worker thread that processes items from a queue in order."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        worker_id: int,
+        work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]],
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        offset_tracker: OffsetTracker,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(daemon=True)
+        self.worker_id = worker_id
+        self.work_queue = work_queue
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.offset_tracker = offset_tracker
+        self.shutdown = False
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        """Process items from the queue in order."""
+        while not self.shutdown:
+            try:
+                work_item = self.work_queue.get()
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+
+            try:
+                with sentry_sdk.start_transaction(
+                    op="queue_worker.process",
+                    name=f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}",
+                ):
+                    self.result_processor(self.identifier, work_item.result)
+
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception(
+                    "Unexpected error in queue worker", extra={"worker_id": self.worker_id}
+                )
+            finally:
+                self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+                metrics.gauge(
+                    "remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth",
+                    self.work_queue.qsize(),
+                    tags={
+                        "identifier": self.identifier,
+                    },
+                )
+
+
+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Fixed pool of queues that guarantees order within groups.
+
+    Key properties:
+    - Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue
+    - Each queue has exactly one worker thread
+    - Items within a queue are processed in FIFO order
+    - No dynamic reassignment that could break ordering
+    - Tracks offset completion for safe commits
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        num_queues: int = 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.num_queues = num_queues
+        self.offset_tracker = OffsetTracker()
+        self.queues: list[queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]]] = []
+        self.workers: list[OrderedQueueWorker[T]] = []
+
+        for i in range(num_queues):
+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,
+                identifier=identifier,
+                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
+            )
+            worker.start()
+            self.workers.append(worker)
+
+    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
+        """
+        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
+        """
+        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues
+
+    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
+        """
+        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
+        """
+        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
+        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]
+
+        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+        work_queue.put(work_item)
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Get statistics about queue depths."""
+        queue_depths = [q.qsize() for q in self.queues]
+        return {
+            "queue_depths": queue_depths,
+            "total_items": sum(queue_depths),
+        }
+
+    def wait_until_empty(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bool:
+        """Wait until all queues are empty. Returns True if successful, False if timeout."""
+        start_time = time.time()
+        while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
+            if self.get_stats()["total_items"] == 0:
+                return True
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        return False
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        """Gracefully shutdown all workers."""
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.shutdown = True
+
+        for q in self.queues:
+            try:
+                q.shutdown(immediate=False)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error shutting down queue")
+
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.join(timeout=5.0)
+
+
+class SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy(ProcessingStrategy[KafkaPayload], Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Processing strategy that uses a fixed pool of queues.
+
+    Guarantees:
+    - Items for the same group are processed in order
+    - No item is lost or processed out of order
+    - Natural backpressure when queues fill up
+    - Only commits offsets after successful processing
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        queue_pool: FixedQueuePool[T],
+        decoder: Callable[[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], T | None],
+        grouping_fn: Callable[[T], str],
+        commit_function: Callable[[dict[Partition, int]], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self.queue_pool = queue_pool
+        self.decoder = decoder
+        self.grouping_fn = grouping_fn
+        self.commit_function = commit_function
+        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
+
+        self.commit_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._commit_loop, daemon=True)
+        self.commit_thread.start()
+
+    def _commit_loop(self) -> None:
+        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
+            try:
+                self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)
+
+                committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()
+
+                if committable:
+                    metrics.incr(
+                        "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed",
+                        len(committable),
+                        tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+                    )
+
+                    self.commit_function(committable)
+                    for partition, offset in committable.items():
+                        self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.mark_committed(partition, offset)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error in commit loop")
+
+    def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
+        try:
+            result = self.decoder(message.payload)
+
+            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
+            partition = message.value.partition
+            offset = message.value.offset
+
+            if result is None:
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
+                return
+
+            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)
+
+            work_item = WorkItem(
+                partition=partition,
+                offset=offset,
+                result=result,
+                message=message,
+            )
+
+            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)
+
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")
+            if isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue):
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+
+    def poll(self) -> None:
+        stats = self.queue_pool.get_stats()
+        metrics.gauge(
+            "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued",
+            stats["total_items"],
+            tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def terminate(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def join(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
+        self.close()

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: In OrderedQueueWorker.run, the finally block calls self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...) regardless of whether result_processor raised, so a message whose processing threw is marked complete and its offset is committed by the commit loop (offset+1). WHY: The strategy guarantees it 'Only commits offsets after successful processing'; completing on failure silently drops the failed message (Kafka will not redeliver it because the offset advanced), causing permanent data loss for any processor that raises. HOW: Only complete the offset on success, e.g. set a success flag inside the try and call complete_offset in the finally only when success is True (or move complete_offset out of finally to after the successful call), leaving the offset outstanding (and thus blocking commits) on error.
