+
+import logging
+import queue
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import defaultdict
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar
+
+import sentry_sdk
+from arroyo.backends.kafka.consumer import KafkaPayload
+from arroyo.processing.strategies import ProcessingStrategy
+from arroyo.types import BrokerValue, FilteredPayload, Message, Partition
+
+from sentry.utils import metrics
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):
+    """Work item that includes the original message for offset tracking."""
+
+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T
+    message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]
+
+
+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:
+                        break
+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable
+
+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}
+
+
+class OrderedQueueWorker(threading.Thread, Generic[T]):
+    """Worker thread that processes items from a queue in order."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        worker_id: int,
+        work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]],
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        offset_tracker: OffsetTracker,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(daemon=True)
+        self.worker_id = worker_id
+        self.work_queue = work_queue
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.offset_tracker = offset_tracker
+        self.shutdown = False
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        """Process items from the queue in order."""
+        while not self.shutdown:
+            try:
+                work_item = self.work_queue.get()
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+
+            try:
+                with sentry_sdk.start_transaction(
+                    op="queue_worker.process",
+                    name=f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}",
+                ):
+                    self.result_processor(self.identifier, work_item.result)
+
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception(
+                    "Unexpected error in queue worker", extra={"worker_id": self.worker_id}
+                )
+            finally:
+                self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+                metrics.gauge(
+                    "remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth",
+                    self.work_queue.qsize(),
+                    tags={
+                        "identifier": self.identifier,
+                    },
+                )
+
+
+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Fixed pool of queues that guarantees order within groups.
+
+    Key properties:
+    - Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue
+    - Each queue has exactly one worker thread
+    - Items within a queue are processed in FIFO order
+    - No dynamic reassignment that could break ordering
+    - Tracks offset completion for safe commits
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        num_queues: int = 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.num_queues = num_queues
+        self.offset_tracker = OffsetTracker()
+        self.queues: list[queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]]] = []
+        self.workers: list[OrderedQueueWorker[T]] = []
+
+        for i in range(num_queues):
+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,
+                identifier=identifier,
+                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
+            )
+            worker.start()
+            self.workers.append(worker)
+
+    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
+        """
+        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
+        """
+        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues
+
+    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
+        """
+        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
+        """
+        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
+        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]
+
+        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+        work_queue.put(work_item)
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Get statistics about queue depths."""
+        queue_depths = [q.qsize() for q in self.queues]
+        return {
+            "queue_depths": queue_depths,
+            "total_items": sum(queue_depths),
+        }
+
+    def wait_until_empty(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bool:
+        """Wait until all queues are empty. Returns True if successful, False if timeout."""
+        start_time = time.time()
+        while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
+            if self.get_stats()["total_items"] == 0:
+                return True
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        return False
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        """Gracefully shutdown all workers."""
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.shutdown = True
+
+        for q in self.queues:
+            try:
+                q.shutdown(immediate=False)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error shutting down queue")
+
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.join(timeout=5.0)
+
+
+class SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy(ProcessingStrategy[KafkaPayload], Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Processing strategy that uses a fixed pool of queues.
+
+    Guarantees:
+    - Items for the same group are processed in order
+    - No item is lost or processed out of order
+    - Natural backpressure when queues fill up
+    - Only commits offsets after successful processing
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        queue_pool: FixedQueuePool[T],
+        decoder: Callable[[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], T | None],
+        grouping_fn: Callable[[T], str],
+        commit_function: Callable[[dict[Partition, int]], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self.queue_pool = queue_pool
+        self.decoder = decoder
+        self.grouping_fn = grouping_fn
+        self.commit_function = commit_function
+        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
+
+        self.commit_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._commit_loop, daemon=True)
+        self.commit_thread.start()
+
+    def _commit_loop(self) -> None:
+        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
+            try:
+                self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)
+
+                committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()
+
+                if committable:
+                    metrics.incr(
+                        "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed",
+                        len(committable),
+                        tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+                    )
+
+                    self.commit_function(committable)
+                    for partition, offset in committable.items():
+                        self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.mark_committed(partition, offset)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error in commit loop")
+
+    def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
+        try:
+            result = self.decoder(message.payload)
+
+            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
+            partition = message.value.partition
+            offset = message.value.offset
+
+            if result is None:
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
+                return
+
+            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)
+
+            work_item = WorkItem(
+                partition=partition,
+                offset=offset,
+                result=result,
+                message=message,
+            )
+
+            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)
+
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")
+            if isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue):
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+
+    def poll(self) -> None:
+        stats = self.queue_pool.get_stats()
+        metrics.gauge(
+            "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued",
+            stats["total_items"],
+            tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def terminate(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def join(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
+        self.close()

+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from types import ModuleType
+from typing import Any
+
+from rest_framework.request import Request
+
+from sentry import options
+from sentry.models.organization import Organization
+from sentry.search.events.types import SnubaParams
+
+
+def is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(
+    snuba_params: SnubaParams,
+    organization: Organization,
+    dataset: ModuleType,
+    request: Request,
+) -> bool:
+    """
+    Determine if this query should use error upsampling transformations.
+    Only applies when ALL projects are allowlisted and we're querying error events.
+    """
+    if not _are_all_projects_error_upsampled(snuba_params.project_ids, organization):
+        return False
+
+    return _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)
+
+
+def _are_all_projects_error_upsampled(
+    project_ids: Sequence[int], organization: Organization
+) -> bool:
+    """
+    Check if ALL projects in the query are allowlisted for error upsampling.
+    Only returns True if all projects pass the allowlist condition.
+    """
+    if not project_ids:
+        return False
+
+    allowlist = options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])
+    if not allowlist:
+        return False
+
+    # All projects must be in the allowlist
+    result = all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)
+    return result
+
+
+def transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(
+    query_columns: Sequence[str],
+) -> list[str]:
+    """
+    Transform aggregation functions to use sum(sample_weight) instead of count()
+    for error upsampling. Only called when all projects are allowlisted.
+    """
+    transformed_columns = []
+    for column in query_columns:
+        column_lower = column.lower().strip()
+
+        if column_lower == "count()":
+            # Simple count becomes sum of sample weights
+            transformed_columns.append("upsampled_count() as count")
+
+        else:
+            transformed_columns.append(column)
+
+    return transformed_columns
+
+
+def _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset: Any, request: Request) -> bool:
+    """
+    Determine if we should apply sample_weight transformations based on the dataset
+    and query context. Only apply for error events since sample_weight doesn't exist
+    for transactions.
+    """
+    from sentry.snuba import discover, errors
+
+    # Always apply for the errors dataset
+    if dataset == errors:
+        return True
+
+    from sentry.snuba import transactions
+
+    # Never apply for the transactions dataset
+    if dataset == transactions:
+        return False
+
+    # For the discover dataset, check if we're querying errors specifically
+    if dataset == discover:
+        result = _is_error_focused_query(request)
+        return result
+
+    # For other datasets (spans, metrics, etc.), don't apply
+    return False
+
+
+def _is_error_focused_query(request: Request) -> bool:
+    """
+    Check if a query is focused on error events.
+    Reduced to only check for event.type:error to err on the side of caution.
+    """
+    query = request.GET.get("query", "").lower()
+
+    if "event.type:error" in query:
+        return True
+
+    return False

WHY: For inputs whose sanitized form is shorter but shares an overlapping run at both ends (e.g. value="aaa" vs sanitized="aa", giving start=2 and end=2), `value.length()-end = 1 < start = 2`, so `substring(2,1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, aborting the verifier with an unhandled exception instead of reporting the offending key. HOW: Clamp the indices, e.g. compute `int from = Math.min(start, value.length()-end); int to = Math.max(from, value.length()-end);` (and the same for sanitized) before taking the substring.

gold.comment: The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: TotalDocs iterates b.cache at bleve.go:146 without holding cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes to the same map at bleve.go:138 under the lock. Before this PR the entire BuildIndex function held cacheMu.Lock, serializing the write with TotalDocs; the finer-grained lock now permits a Go map read/write race during Prometheus collection. Make TotalDocs acquire cacheMu.RLock before reading b.cache.

gold.comment: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: TagDevice now returns ErrDeviceLimitReached to make Authenticate reject the request, but tagDeviceUI has already written the device's cache key (localCache.SetDefault at line 87) before CreateOrUpdateDevice fails. The next request from the same device gets a cache hit, tagDeviceUI returns nil, and anonymous authentication succeeds, so a device over the limit only fails once and then gets in for 29 minutes. Remove the cache entry when CreateOrUpdateDevice fails, or only set it after a successful write.

WHY: this writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into `credential.key`; the very next instantiation calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) and now fails because scope/token_type/expiry_date/access_token/refresh_token are no longer at the top level, permanently breaking the Google Calendar credential after the first token refresh. HOW: use `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;` (or revert to `googleCredentialSchema.parse`).

gold.comment: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: The new backup-code branch is checked before TOTP, but the password check above it (line 121) only runs when `credentials.totpCode` is empty. So a request with any non-empty dummy `totpCode` plus a valid `backupCode` skips the password check, and TOTP is never verified either. An attacker who has a leaked backup code and the email can log in without the account password; fix this by always verifying the password when a backupCode is supplied, or by rejecting requests that send both totpCode and backupCode.

gold.comment: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

gold.comment: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Success is checked with `response.statusText !== "OK"`. statusText is empty on HTTP/2 and some runtimes, so valid 200 responses are treated as errors and throw an HttpError. Fix: check `response.ok` instead.

deterministic.existingCode: if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });

gold.comment: The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw request input `guests` as the `newGuests` argument instead of the `uniqueGuests` that was explicitly computed after dedup/blacklist filtering. WHY: email-manager.ts:541 uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to pick the template, so an email in `guests` that already belongs to an existing attendee (or a blacklisted address) is misclassified as a newly added guest and receives the wrong email (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification). HOW: pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

deterministic.existingCode: await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);

gold.comment: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The start-bound check only rejects slots that end at or before the override start; it never checks whether the slot starts before the override. WHY: A slot that begins before the override window and ends inside it is treated as available, so fixed hosts can be booked partly outside their override hours. HOW: Reject the slot when slotStartTime is before the override start.

gold.comment: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Computed keys using Zod schema objects' toString() do not define dynamic properties, and this z.object strips actual expiry fields such as expires_in and expiry_date. With syncing enabled, Zoom subsequently computes expiry_date from missing newTokens.expires_in, producing NaN, while Office365 loses its refreshed expiry. Define the supported expiry properties explicitly and preserve required provider fields with passthrough or a suitable catchall.

gold.comment: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the user, so tRPC returns a 500 instead of a structured FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: A plain `Error` is thrown when the credential is missing or not owned by the user. tRPC turns this into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and logs it as a server fault, instead of returning a proper client error. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found or access denied" })` (or FORBIDDEN) instead.

gold.comment: Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: When a caller embeds the result as `WHERE ${base} AND <extra>`, SQL operator precedence turns it into `A OR (B AND extra)`, which can leak rows outside the authorization scope or ignore the extra predicate. Always wrap the fragment `getBaseConditions` returns in parentheses, using `Prisma.sql` for `authConditions` and `filterConditions`, and wrap the eventTypeId OR-fragment in its own parentheses.

gold.comment: After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent:
WHAT: After fetching and persisting a new access token, the `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` (the pre-refresh value) rather than the just-obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.
WHY: The connection that this block refreshes for is authenticated with the stale/expired token it was supposed to replace, so the refresh has no effect on the returned connection and requests can fail with an expired session.
HOW: Use the refreshed token when building the connection, e.g. `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

gold.comment: The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The webhook indexes appStoreMetadata using the database app slug, but that map is keyed by integration directory names. For example, Google credentials use appId 'google-calendar' while apps.metadata.generated.ts exposes the metadata under 'googlecalendar', so a valid Google sync request returns 404. Resolve the metadata by its slug value instead of assuming the map key equals the database slug.

+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):

+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T

+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:
+                        break
+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable

+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}

+class OrderedQueueWorker(threading.Thread, Generic[T]):

+

+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Fixed pool of queues that guarantees order within groups.
+
+    Key properties:
+    - Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue
+    - Each queue has exactly one worker thread
+    - Items within a queue are processed in FIFO order
+    - No dynamic reassignment that could break ordering
+    - Tracks offset completion for safe commits
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        num_queues: int = 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.num_queues = num_queues
+        self.offset_tracker = OffsetTracker()
+        self.queues: list[queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]]] = []
+        self.workers: list[OrderedQueueWorker[T]] = []
+
+        for i in range(num_queues):
+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,
+                identifier=identifier,
+                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
+            )
+            worker.start()
+            self.workers.append(worker)
+
+    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
+        """
+        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
+        """
+        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues

+    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
+        """

+        """

+        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]
+
+        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+        work_queue.put(work_item)
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:

+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T

+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed

+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:

+                if highest_committable > last_committed:

+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):

+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The restarted-path kill guard `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` is always False for the processes this class creates, because they come from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` (as the annotation on line 68 states), which is not a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process`.
WHY: When a flusher process crashes or hangs, `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement for the same shards while the previous process is never killed (`process.kill()` is skipped) and is never joined; for the hang case the stuck process is still alive and can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, producing duplicate segments to buffered-segments. This is a regression: the pre-PR code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, which worked for these spawn processes.
HOW: Guard against the actual type, e.g. `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess): process.kill()` (or `hasattr(process, "kill")`), and/or compare against the same base class used to build it, so spawned processes are killed before replacement.

finding.suggestionContent: The new validation-failure warning logs `raw_report`, the full unvalidated report object supplied by the caller. gold.comment: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

gold.comment: The cache 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale instead of the user's locale, so non-US users see US-style dates in an otherwise translated label.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

gold.comment: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The legacy half of Mode 3 is never verified, so these tests cannot catch its removal. Mode 3 is documented as writing to BOTH LegacyStorage and Storage, and the implementation performs the legacy write in a detached goroutine (`go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57, and likewise at 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Each test registers legacy expectations (`setupLegacyFn`, e.g. lines 30-32 and 40-42) but never calls `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled` or `AssertNumberOfCalls`, and never waits for or observes the goroutine — no channel, no polling. Additionally `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (lines 53-54, and the same pair in every other test function) share one `*mock.Mock`, so even a count assertion could not distinguish a legacy call from a storage call. Deleting every `d.Legacy.*` call from the implementation leaves all six tests passing, which is exactly the regression the names — and the Mode 3 contract — claim to cover.

gold.comment: Leftover debug logs in the annotation cleanup emit Error-level entries with the full ID list on every batch, flooding error logs during normal operation.

finding.label: performance
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: Normal, successful per-batch cleanup activity is logged with `r.log.Error(...)` in all three flows (lines 534/537, 554/557, 576/579), including `"err", err` where err is provably nil (it was already checked non-nil above). WHY: These emit ERROR-level log entries (and large `ids` slices) on every successful batch, so error logs/metrics are polluted with false errors on every cleanup cycle and the actual error signal is buried. HOW: Downgrade these to `r.log.Debug`/`r.log.Info` and stop passing the nil `err`, keeping `r.log.Error` only for real failures.

gold.comment: Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The async legacy Create goroutine derives its context from the request ctx, which is cancelled when the HTTP handler returns. The legacy write is then likely cancelled or aborted before it completes, so legacy storage silently misses writes. The same pattern is in Delete (108-114), Update (134-141) and DeleteCollection (161-167). Fix: derive the timeout context from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (Go 1.21+) so it keeps the values but not the request cancellation.

gold.comment: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import queue
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import defaultdict
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar
+
+import sentry_sdk
+from arroyo.backends.kafka.consumer import KafkaPayload
+from arroyo.processing.strategies import ProcessingStrategy
+from arroyo.types import BrokerValue, FilteredPayload, Message, Partition
+
+from sentry.utils import metrics
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):
+    """Work item that includes the original message for offset tracking."""
+
+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T
+    message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]
+
+
+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.
+
+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.all_offsets: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.outstanding: dict[Partition, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)
+
+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.outstanding[partition].discard(offset)
+
+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:
+        """
+        Get the highest offset per partition that can be safely committed.
+
+        For each partition, finds the highest contiguous offset that has been processed.
+        """
+        committable = {}
+        for partition in list(self.all_offsets.keys()):
+            with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+                all_offsets = self.all_offsets[partition]
+                if not all_offsets:
+                    continue
+
+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)
+
+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)
+
+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)
+
+                highest_committable = last_committed
+                for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):
+                    if offset in all_offsets and offset not in outstanding:
+                        highest_committable = offset
+                    else:
+                        break
+
+                if highest_committable > last_committed:
+                    committable[partition] = highest_committable
+
+        return committable
+
+    def mark_committed(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Update the last committed offset for a partition."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.last_committed[partition] = offset
+            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
+            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}
+
+
+class OrderedQueueWorker(threading.Thread, Generic[T]):
+    """Worker thread that processes items from a queue in order."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        worker_id: int,
+        work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]],
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        offset_tracker: OffsetTracker,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(daemon=True)
+        self.worker_id = worker_id
+        self.work_queue = work_queue
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.offset_tracker = offset_tracker
+        self.shutdown = False
+
+    def run(self) -> None:
+        """Process items from the queue in order."""
+        while not self.shutdown:
+            try:
+                work_item = self.work_queue.get()
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+
+            try:
+                with sentry_sdk.start_transaction(
+                    op="queue_worker.process",
+                    name=f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}",
+                ):
+                    self.result_processor(self.identifier, work_item.result)
+
+            except queue.ShutDown:
+                break
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception(
+                    "Unexpected error in queue worker", extra={"worker_id": self.worker_id}
+                )
+            finally:
+                self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+                metrics.gauge(
+                    "remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth",
+                    self.work_queue.qsize(),
+                    tags={
+                        "identifier": self.identifier,
+                    },
+                )
+
+
+class FixedQueuePool(Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Fixed pool of queues that guarantees order within groups.
+
+    Key properties:
+    - Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue
+    - Each queue has exactly one worker thread
+    - Items within a queue are processed in FIFO order
+    - No dynamic reassignment that could break ordering
+    - Tracks offset completion for safe commits
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        result_processor: Callable[[str, T], None],
+        identifier: str,
+        num_queues: int = 20,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.result_processor = result_processor
+        self.identifier = identifier
+        self.num_queues = num_queues
+        self.offset_tracker = OffsetTracker()
+        self.queues: list[queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]]] = []
+        self.workers: list[OrderedQueueWorker[T]] = []
+
+        for i in range(num_queues):
+            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue()
+            self.queues.append(work_queue)
+
+            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
+                worker_id=i,
+                work_queue=work_queue,
+                result_processor=result_processor,
+                identifier=identifier,
+                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
+            )
+            worker.start()
+            self.workers.append(worker)
+
+    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
+        """
+        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
+        """
+        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues
+
+    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
+        """
+        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
+        """
+        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
+        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]
+
+        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
+        work_queue.put(work_item)
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Get statistics about queue depths."""
+        queue_depths = [q.qsize() for q in self.queues]
+        return {
+            "queue_depths": queue_depths,
+            "total_items": sum(queue_depths),
+        }
+
+    def wait_until_empty(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bool:
+        """Wait until all queues are empty. Returns True if successful, False if timeout."""
+        start_time = time.time()
+        while time.time() - start_time < timeout:
+            if self.get_stats()["total_items"] == 0:
+                return True
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        return False
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        """Gracefully shutdown all workers."""
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.shutdown = True
+
+        for q in self.queues:
+            try:
+                q.shutdown(immediate=False)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error shutting down queue")
+
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.join(timeout=5.0)
+
+
+class SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy(ProcessingStrategy[KafkaPayload], Generic[T]):
+    """
+    Processing strategy that uses a fixed pool of queues.
+
+    Guarantees:
+    - Items for the same group are processed in order
+    - No item is lost or processed out of order
+    - Natural backpressure when queues fill up
+    - Only commits offsets after successful processing
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        queue_pool: FixedQueuePool[T],
+        decoder: Callable[[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload], T | None],
+        grouping_fn: Callable[[T], str],
+        commit_function: Callable[[dict[Partition, int]], None],
+    ) -> None:
+        self.queue_pool = queue_pool
+        self.decoder = decoder
+        self.grouping_fn = grouping_fn
+        self.commit_function = commit_function
+        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
+
+        self.commit_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._commit_loop, daemon=True)
+        self.commit_thread.start()
+
+    def _commit_loop(self) -> None:
+        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
+            try:
+                self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)
+
+                committable = self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.get_committable_offsets()
+
+                if committable:
+                    metrics.incr(
+                        "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.offsets_committed",
+                        len(committable),
+                        tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+                    )
+
+                    self.commit_function(committable)
+                    for partition, offset in committable.items():
+                        self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.mark_committed(partition, offset)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Error in commit loop")
+
+    def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
+        try:
+            result = self.decoder(message.payload)
+
+            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
+            partition = message.value.partition
+            offset = message.value.offset
+
+            if result is None:
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
+                return
+
+            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)
+
+            work_item = WorkItem(
+                partition=partition,
+                offset=offset,
+                result=result,
+                message=message,
+            )
+
+            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)
+
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")
+            if isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue):
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(
+                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
+                )
+
+    def poll(self) -> None:
+        stats = self.queue_pool.get_stats()
+        metrics.gauge(
+            "remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued",
+            stats["total_items"],
+            tags={"identifier": self.queue_pool.identifier},
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def terminate(self) -> None:
+        self.shutdown_event.set()
+        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
+
+    def join(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
+        self.close()

gold.comment: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates group resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), but individual group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never get their type set to "Groups" — getOrCreateResource calls resourceStore.create(...) (which takes no type) and never calls resource.setType(...), whereas only the all-groups resource gets setType("Groups") in AdminPermissionsSchema.init (line 274); V1 sets it explicitly at GroupPermissions.java:117 (`groupResource.setType("Group")`). As a result findByType returns none of the per-group resources, so a caller's per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are never enumerated and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns an empty/incorrect set. This makes UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource's group-based user restriction (which feed the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute) return wrong results for fine-grained admins. Set the resource type to "Groups" when creating individual group resources (or enumerate via findByName/store lookups instead of type) so that group-scoped permissions are actually discovered.

gold.comment: testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand, so the feature guard in the check subcommand is untested.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The feature-disabled guard added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run has no test coverage while the identical guard in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata is covered by testFeatureNotEnabled. WHY: Removing or breaking the Check guard would not fail any test, leaving the gated command unprotected. HOW: Add a dist-test launch of {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME} without --features asserting the disabled error and exit code 4, mirroring the metadata case.

gold.comment: connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of the feature-flag-aware factory, so cache status is queried and shown even when calendar-cache is disabled.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The handler directly constructs `CalendarCacheRepository` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()`/`initFromCredentialId()`, which checks the `calendar-cache` feature flag and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when disabled. When the feature is off globally, this still executes a `CalendarCache` `groupBy` query on every connectedCalendars call for no benefit and can expose stale cache status. Use the existing `CalendarCache.init*` factory or gate the query with the feature flag.

gold.comment: The graceful-shutdown test only asserts that the factory cleared its queue_pool reference, which shutdown always does, so it does not verify that pending work is drained or workers stop.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: This does not verify graceful shutdown: factory.shutdown unconditionally clears queue_pool after calling pool.shutdown, so the assertion passes even if pending messages are abandoned or worker threads remain alive. Retain the pool reference and assert that all submitted work completed and its workers stopped; the current worker shutdown flag can stop workers without draining their queues.
